title: Fix logging with extcaps
description:
Extcaps require a log file when invoked in child mode. It also has
a specific flag to enable debugging, other that the wslog options.

Fix the logging to:
  1. Enable debug log level if --debug is used.
  2. Do not emit messages to the stderr if debug is enabled.

This brings extcap logging to the same feature level it had before
wslog replaced GLib logging.

notes.body:
@jvalverde I'm sorry, but it made things worst than before by my opinion...
1. Condition in extcap_custom_log() is incorrect by my opinion - it should log to file if defined and to console elsewhere. It should not care about current level. BTW it logged to file only debug level messages, but info and higher were logged to console.
2. You removed calling ws_log_parse_args() from all extcaps. I think it could be usefull.

I'm fixing it in !5291 and I propose to close #17764 with comment I writtend to it. I noted this to extcap documentation.

It did not make things worse because logging was not working and now at least you can use the extcap log file. As I have tried to explain, I just wanted to restore what the original implementers of extcap had done as far as logging goes (and that I broke). I think that was accomplished.

I'm not disagreeing with you that it can be improved beyond that and I encourage you to try to do that.

But it doesn't work now. Try:

`./run/extcap/randpktdump --extcap-interface=randpkt --fifo=FILENAME --capture --debug`

and then

`./run/extcap/randpktdump --extcap-interface=randpkt --fifo=FILENAME --capture --debug --debug-file=/tmp/abc `

First command prints nothing even debug is set. The reason is condition in extcap_custom_log(). Second command prints all output to the file which is correct.

My point of view is that in first case it should same output as in second case, just to console.

You are right that the behavior with --debug is not exactly the same. The reason is that now the log handler is set at startup, where previously it was set later (see [here](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/commit/dc7f0b88bba0c703d9c802b153e145dc6b3dc549#83744a810254dc76fb137d09098bb50ffd015360_149_128)).

So yes, you are right that it is worse in that sense, but that only applies to extcap start-up. The main loop is the same, as far as I can tell from looking at the old code. No debug output anywhere without a log file.

Yes, but I think that no output with --debug makes sense, isn't it? That is original reason why I created !5291.

I propose to accept it and everything would work as I expect. Documentation is updated too to explain consequences of using different debug/log methods with extcap.
Output to the console with --debug makes sense, but only if it works always, including in the main loop. I will look at !5291 again to see how that works, I must have missed it.

I think it does work in !5291 well. There is small "gap" between logging init and command line parsing where the code don't know about set debug. In this "gap" nothing is logged. It can be solved only by --log-level=debug which is parsed sooner than rest of parameters or by setting WIRESHARK_LOG_LEVEL=debug.

But I think this "gap" is very small so we don't have to care about.

BTW your change improved it - you register message handler at beginning.
